Brent and Angela Freeman founded Built For More Institute to help people recognize invisible limits, build trust, intentionally develop their identity, and create better results in life.

In their new book, Identity Determines Income: And Everything Else, they reveal how the identity you carry influences far more than your income. It shapes your beliefs, your decisions, your relationships, the opportunities you recognize, and ultimately, the life you create.

What if the results you’re getting have less to do with how hard you work, and more to do with something you don’t even realize is shaping your life?

And what if changing how you see yourself could change everything else?

Most people try to change from the top down.

More money. Better relationships. More success. But there is a structure behind every result you produce, and it works whether you are aware of it or not.

Your identity, how you see yourself, sits at the foundation. It shapes what you believe is possible. Your beliefs drive your actions. Your actions create your results. And your results reinforce your identity.

This book will help you understand

  • Why identity precedes results.
  • How invisible ceilings can influence what you believe is possible.
  • How beliefs influence actions, and actions influence results.
  • Why awareness must come before meaningful change.
  • How service, trust, relationships, and opportunity connect to income.
  • How to begin intentionally building the identity that supports the life you want to create.

Brent and Angela Freeman

For decades, Brent and Angela have helped people transform their lives while living these principles themselves. They’ve experienced setbacks, disappointment, pressure, and starting over.

Along the way, they’ve watched ordinary people create extraordinary lives, and others with incredible potential remain stuck. They discovered that the difference wasn’t simply what people knew, or what they did. It was who they believed they were.

We wrote this book to help people recognize what may be shaping their results, and understand that what has been does not have to determine what comes next.

For Brent & AngelaCover image now comes from the “PAPERBACK 3” file. The front is unchanged; the new back-cover text, including the bold gold lines, is in the red section just below. Amazon and Audible buttons appear as soon as the listings are live.
  • As you read this book, you will finally understand why your life has produced the results it has.
  • Discover how understanding your identity gives you the power to create different results.
  • Discover what happens when a person decides that being broke, blindsided, and backed into a corner is still not enough to make them quit…

Why do some people seem to create opportunity wherever they go, while others, with the same opportunities, talent, and work ethic, remain stuck?

What if the greatest force shaping your confidence, your relationships, your opportunities, your income, and your future isn’t your education, your circumstances, or even your talent?

What if it’s your identity?

For decades, Brent and Angela Freeman have helped people transform their lives while living these principles themselves. They’ve experienced setbacks, disappointment, pressure, and starting over. Along the way, they’ve watched ordinary people create extraordinary lives, and others with incredible potential remain stuck.

They discovered that the difference wasn’t simply what people knew, or what they did.

It was who they believed they were.

You know what you should do. So why is it sometimes so difficult to do it?

Why do you keep falling into the same habits, making the same choices, or holding yourself back, even when you genuinely want something different?

What if the problem isn’t that you need to work harder? What if something deeper has been shaping your decisions, your confidence, your relationships, your opportunities, and your results all along?

Identity Determines Income: And Everything Else offers a different way to look at personal growth: start with the person you believe yourself to be.

Brent and Angela Freeman show why lasting change isn’t simply about working harder, learning more, setting bigger goals, or finding the perfect strategy. Your identity influences what you believe is possible, the opportunities you pursue, the decisions you make, the standards you accept, and ultimately the results you create.

Drawing from decades of real-world experience in business, sales, leadership, and personal development, as well as their own successes, setbacks, and experiences of starting over, the Freemans combine powerful true stories with practical principles designed to help you recognize the invisible forces that may have been shaping your life.

Inside, you’ll discover how to:

  • Recognize beliefs and patterns that may be limiting your results.
  • Understand the connection between identity, beliefs, actions, and results.
  • Challenge the invisible ceilings influencing what you believe is possible.
  • Build greater confidence, awareness, and personal responsibility.
  • Break patterns of self-sabotage and inconsistency.
  • Understand how values and service build trust, creating relationships and opportunities that can lead to income.
  • Intentionally develop an identity that supports the future you want.
  • Create changes that extend beyond income into relationships, leadership, confidence, and everyday life.

Your current results may tell a story about the identity you’ve built so far. They don’t have to determine the story that comes next.

Fourteen chapters, fourteen laws

Each chapter is built around one law: a single sentence that carries its idea. Every chapter closes with questions for your Identity Journal, and most with a practical exercise. Open any chapter to see a sample.

  1. 1The Identity You Live InIdentity always precedes income.

    The income ceiling always reveals an identity ceiling first.

    Practical exerciseStart your Identity Journal

    A question for your journalWho would I need to become to create the life I truly want?

  2. 2The Invisible CeilingEvery ceiling in life is first accepted in thought.

    The limits you stop questioning eventually become the life you keep recreating.

    A question for your journalWhat would I do differently if I no longer needed anyone’s approval?

  3. 3The Rusty NailPain becomes power the moment it produces decision.

    Remaining the same always has a hidden cost.

    Practical exerciseIdentify What Must Change

    A question for your journalWhat decision am I avoiding?

  4. 4Villains, Victims, or VictorsMeaning determines momentum.

    The meaning you give your pain will often determine the future you create from it.

    Practical exerciseThe Story Shift

    A question for your journalWhat story am I still telling myself about why things have not worked out?

  5. 5The Hidden Structure Behind SuccessPreparation determines performance.

    Practical exerciseSharpening the Axe

    A question for your journalWhere in my life am I working harder instead of sharpening the axe?

  6. 6The Roots of IdentityValues determine direction.

    Values are the roots.

    Practical exerciseDefine Your Identity Roots

    A question for your journalWhat do I say I value, and what do my actions actually prove I value?

  7. 7Responsibility Creates PowerOwnership is the moment power returns to your life.

    Ownership becomes real when it produces action.

    Practical exerciseActivate Ownership

    A question for your journalWhere am I waiting instead of acting?

  8. 8Awareness Creates GrowthGrowth begins the moment you become aware of your effect on other people.

    Practical exerciseThe Pause Principle

    A question for your journalWhat is it like to be on the other side of me?

  9. 9The Power of BeliefYour self-image silently determines the level of action you are willing to take.

    Practical exerciseIdentity Visualization

    A question for your journalWhat opportunity might I pursue differently if my self-image became stronger?

  10. 10The Identity MirrorThe life you are living is a reflection of the identity you are holding.

    Your identity is revealed in the choices you make every day.

    Practical exerciseThe Identity Mirror

    A question for your journalWho am I becoming through my repeated behavior?

  11. 11The HourglassWhat you focus on with the time you have determines the life you create.

    Practical exerciseReclaiming the Sand

    A question for your journalWhat is one “next step” I already know I need to take?

  12. 12Service Creates TrustWhen you consistently act in another person’s best interest, trust compounds over time.

    Trust creates opportunities that money alone never can.

    Practical exerciseMoving Up the Ladder

    A question for your journalWhat am I consistently doing to earn the trust of others?

  13. 13Value Creates IncomeIncome is the result of the value your identity teaches you to see and create.

    Practical exerciseBecoming a Value Creator

    A question for your journalWhat need around me could I begin helping solve immediately?

  14. 14Sales as Service Creates IncomeIncome is maximized when service becomes your standard, not your strategy.

    Identity is not discovered accidentally. It is built intentionally.

    Practical exerciseLiving the Identity Standard

    A question for your journalWhat would this version of me consistently do?

Plus closing thoughts, the Golden Key, and a one-page Identity Commitment.

Introduction

As you read this book, you will finally understand why your life has produced the results it has.

Discover how understanding your identity gives you the power to create different results.

The life you experience tomorrow will be shaped by the identity you build today.

The Day I Realized Identity Shapes Everything

Discover what happens when a person decides that being broke, blindsided, and backed into a corner is still not enough to make them quit… that is the moment pressure stops being your enemy… and starts revealing who you really are.

The identity you bring determines the outcomes you create.

This isn’t a book you’ll finish and someday apply… It’s a book that opens new doors in your mind as you turn the pages.

1

The Identity You Live In

The Trifecta

Before you accept this idea as truth… you should see it in real life. Not once. But multiple times.

Got Me Under Pressure

I had a good friend in sales, a man of real integrity. We had worked together before, and I trusted him.

One afternoon, we were talking about business when he asked if I would be interested in forming a joint venture company with him and his two partners.

The idea sounded promising. They were building a company around packaging and media production, and they needed help developing the product. I agreed to talk. Before long, I became deeply involved.

I ended up writing the material, doing the research and development, and helping shape the entire product from the ground up. I didn’t mind the work. I believed in what we were building.

But there were signs early on that something wasn’t right.

One of the partners, the CEO, was hard-driving, pushy, and cutthroat. The CFO was a complete “yes man.” Whatever the CEO wanted, the CEO got.

He knew exactly what to do. He knew how to market it. He knew how to sell it. He knew how to structure it. He knew everything.

There was only one problem. Most of the time, he was talking with great confidence about things he had never actually done.

Eventually, the product was ready. But they couldn’t find anyone to sell it. So the CEO turned to me and essentially said: “You’re the one.”

That meant I was no longer just helping build it. Now I had to carry it. And not in a way I was comfortable with.

This required extensive travel and live seminar selling from a stage in front of large crowds. I had sold one-on-one. I had sold face-to-face. I had sold business-to-business. But standing on a stage in front of hundreds of people and trying to close sales in a live seminar? I had never done that in my life.

Of course, the CEO assured me not to worry. He said he knew exactly how it should be done. There was just one huge problem. He had never done it before.

Then came my first live presentation. Forty-five minutes. That was the longest forty-five minutes of my life.

I walked onto the stage and looked out over a sea of 379 people. All of them were staring at me, waiting to hear about this great opportunity.

Then the microphone stopped working.

Where the book ends, The Key begins

The book closes by handing you a Golden Key: the ability to choose which doors you open and which direction your life takes. The Key is where you learn to use it.

You bring everything with you. Your successes, your disappointments, your strengths, your mistakes, and the things you’re still figuring out. This isn’t about starting over. It’s about building from where you are.

For Brent & AngelaPard’s new key image, beside this section as you asked, without the red shirt in the background.

How each step works

A true story
Brent and Angela share moments from their own lives, from a lawyer friend let go without warning to Brent learning to walk again after five weeks in the hospital.
An idea to hold onto
One clear principle you can recognize the next time it shows up in your day.
Something to try
A short exercise for real life: a conversation, a promise kept, a moment you catch yourself doing something right.
Your Identity Journal
The journal the book asks you to start in Chapter 1. Each step ends with a few questions to answer while the day is still fresh. Over time, the entries become your evidence.

One suggestion before you begin: read some of it out loud, somewhere quiet. Sometimes the words we need most are the ones we finally hear ourselves say.

The eleven steps

Each step builds on the one before it, so they’re meant to be taken in order. Open any step to see what’s inside and the questions you’ll answer in your Identity Journal.

  1. 1The Power of the PauseCreate a pause between what happens and what you do next, so you choose your response instead of reacting.

    Inside this step

    • Recognize the signals
    • Check your compass
    • Now choose
    • Catch yourself doing right

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • Did I react, or did I pause and choose?
    • What did I do right?
    • What does this experience teach me about who I’m becoming?
  2. 2Get the Right Things RightNot everything. The things that matter. Decide what deserves your time, attention, energy, and action.

    Inside this step

    • Look in the mirror
    • What deserves your attention?
    • Use what you already have
    • Recognize and reward progress

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did I do right today?
    • What did I learn?
    • What deserves my attention tomorrow?
  3. 3Doing What You Say MattersMake your actions agree with what you say matters, starting with the promises you make to yourself.

    Inside this step

    • The crossroads
    • Act. Don’t react.
    • Your word to yourself
    • What’s really stopping you?

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What action did I commit to?
    • Did I follow through?
    • If I hesitated, what was really going on?
  4. 4Look Beneath the ActionFind the belief, fear, or story underneath a reaction, including the fear of what other people might think.

    Inside this step

    • Whose voice is that?
    • Fear has a voice: FOPO and FOMO
    • Pause. Breathe. Filter. Choose. Act.
    • Put it on the table

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What belief, fear, or story did I find?
    • Where do I think it came from?
    • Is it still helping me?
  5. 5Build EvidenceConfidence doesn’t have to come first. Start with what’s already true and collect proof of who you’re becoming.

    Inside this step

    • Start with what’s already true
    • Don’t wait for the big win
    • Don’t borrow somebody else’s scorecard
    • Your Evidence File

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did that give me evidence of?
    • What strength did I use?
    • Where did I notice myself becoming more confident or capable?
  6. 6Become What You PracticePractice the person you want to become in ordinary moments, when it’s easy and when it’s hard.

    Inside this step

    • What are you rehearsing?
    • When you slip
    • Consistency isn’t perfection
    • Choose your practice

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did I practice today?
    • Where did I catch myself doing it right?
    • Where did I drift back into an old pattern?
  7. 7What’s It Like to Be on the Other Side of Me?Turn the chair around and look at what other people experience from you.

    Inside this step

    • Turn the camera around
    • Listen for more than words
    • Understanding isn’t agreement
    • The Identity Mirror

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did I bring into the moment?
    • What do I think it was like on the other side of me?
  8. 8Put Service Into ActionNotice the person in front of you and offer something you already have, without keeping score.

    Inside this step

    • Start by noticing
    • You already have something to give
    • Service doesn’t mean saying yes to everything
    • Don’t keep score

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • Where did I put service into action today?
    • What did I notice about the other person?
  9. 9Become Someone People Can TrustTrust doesn’t announce itself. It demonstrates itself, especially when nobody is watching.

    Inside this step

    • Your word has weight
    • Don’t promise what you can’t deliver
    • When nobody is watching
    • When you get it wrong

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did I do today that showed I could be counted on?
    • What do I want my word to mean to the people who know me?
  10. 10When Life Pushes BackWhen the road changes, deal with where you are and find your next available step.

    Inside this step

    • Deal with where you are
    • Don’t confuse your direction with your route
    • When the setback is your fault
    • The next available step

    Questions for your Identity Journal

    • What did I handle well today?
    • What is still within my control?
    • What is my next step?
  11. 11Keep BecomingLook back at how far you’ve come, and decide what you’ll carry forward.

    Inside this step

    • Look at you now
    • Something we haven’t told you
    • The door

A tool you’ll carry with you

Step 4 introduces five words for the moment between what happens and what you do next. By Step 7, you’re using them with other people, too.

  1. Pause.
  2. Breathe.
  3. Filter.
  4. Choose.
  5. Act.

Along the way, you’ll watch for mile markers. Not to measure how far you still have to go, but to remind you how far you’ve already come.

Coaching with Brent and Angela

Sometimes you know where you want to go, but a guide can help you see your next step more clearly.

Brent and Angela work with you personally: walking beside you, helping you discover new possibilities, recognize blind spots, develop your strengths, and keep building a life of significance and success.

Apply for coachingFor teams and organizations

What coaching helps you do

  • Reflect honestly on where you are right now.
  • Clarify what matters most to you.
  • Recognize the beliefs, fears, and blind spots that keep you stuck.
  • Build on the strengths you already have.
  • Create an action plan you can actually follow.

Coaching builds on the principles in Identity Determines Income and The Key, applied to your own work, income, and relationships. Your circumstances and decisions stay your own.

Who you’ll work with

For more than twenty-five years, Brent and Angela have worked together helping individuals and organizations improve communication, leadership, confidence, relationships, and personal growth.

Their backgrounds span sales, training, business development, real estate education, stock market investing education, and transformational identity coaching. The most important lessons, they say, came through adversity and starting over.

Brent and Angela Freeman

Brent and Angela are the founders of Built For More Institute and co-authors of Identity Determines Income: And Everything Else. Drawing from decades of experience in business, sales, leadership, and personal development, they help people recognize invisible limits, build trust, intentionally develop their identity, and create better results in life.

For Brent & AngelaThis photo is 450 pixels square (the 1.5-inch print crop). If you have the full-size original, we can show it larger. A photo of each of you on your own would also help here and for podcasts and press.

Brent Freeman

Brent Freeman is a sales professional, trainer, speaker, coach, and lifelong student of personal growth whose career has spanned decades in sales, leadership, communication, business development, real estate education, stock market investing education, and transformational identity coaching.

Throughout his career, Brent has worked with individuals, sales professionals, business owners, and organizations, helping them improve their communication, strengthen relationships, increase sales, and create better results.

But the greatest lessons he has learned did not come from success alone. They came through adversity, disappointment, betrayal, financial setbacks, and starting over. Those experiences taught him something he has never forgotten: people do not create lasting change simply by learning new information. They create lasting change by becoming a new person.

Angela Freeman

Angela Freeman has extensive experience in sales, coaching, communication, personal development, real estate education, stock market investing education, and transformational identity coaching. For more than twenty-five years, Angela and Brent have worked together helping individuals and organizations improve communication, leadership, confidence, relationships, and personal growth.

Growing up on a small farm, working two jobs, and believing her opportunities were limited, she discovered firsthand that changing the way she saw herself changed the direction of her life. Her story, From Caterpillar to Butterfly, is in Chapter 1.

She believes every person has unique value, untapped potential, and the ability to create a better future when they begin living from a stronger identity.

“You are a true example of how identity determines income and everything else.”From Brent’s dedication of the book to Angela

Why we wrote this book

We did not write this book because we believe we have all the answers. We wrote it because we have spent a lifetime asking questions.

Questions about why some people rise while others remain stuck. Why some people create opportunity while others continually miss it. Why two people can begin with similar circumstances yet build completely different futures.

Over the years, through our own successes, failures, disappointments, and victories, we discovered that the greatest transformation rarely begins by changing circumstances. It begins by changing identity.

Our hope is that Identity Determines Income helps you recognize your own worth, strengthen your identity, and create a future filled with greater purpose, stronger relationships, meaningful opportunities, and lasting contribution.

More than anything, we hope this book reminds you that your past does not have to determine your future. You have the ability to become more than you have been, to create more than you thought possible, and to build a better future, not only for yourself, but for everyone your life touches.

Brent and Angela

Built For More Institute

Brent and Angela founded Built For More Institute to help people transform their identity and, with it, their lives. It publishes the book, offers The Key course, and provides coaching, speaking, training, and workshops.

Privacy

Last updated November 5, 2026

For Brent & AngelaUpdated for this version: forms now save to Content Creator Machine instead of Mailchimp or your email app. This is plain-language wording, not legal advice; please read it before launch and tell Gary anything that isn’t accurate.

Email list

When you sign up for the free chapter, The Key waitlist, or launch news, we save your email address in Content Creator Machine, the system we use for our contacts and email. We use it only to send what you asked for and occasional news from Built For More Institute. Every email has an unsubscribe link. We never sell or share your information.

Coaching applications and messages

When you apply for coaching or ask about speaking, workshops, or group copies, we save what you send (your name, email address, phone number if you give one, and your answers) in Content Creator Machine so Brent and Angela can reply and keep track of the conversation. We use it only for that. If our form can’t send, the website offers to open your email app instead, and that message goes to info@builtformoreinstitute.com.

The assessment

To take Discover Your Next Move, you give us your first name and email address. When you finish, we save your first name, email address, answers, and results in Content Creator Machine so we can email you your results and check in with you once after 30 days. We send you other news only if you tick the box asking for it. Your personal commitment notes are never sent; they stay on your device.

If you print your results or download them as a PDF or Word file, that copy is yours alone.

Who helps us

This website is hosted by Cloudflare. Our contacts and email are managed in Content Creator Machine.

Analytics

We may use privacy-friendly analytics to count visits. We don’t use advertising trackers.

Questions

Write to info@builtformoreinstitute.com to ask what we hold about you or to have it deleted.

The Identity Journal

Chapter 1 asks you to start an Identity Journal. Here’s one ready for you: the reflection questions for every chapter of the book, with room to write your answers.

  • Reflection questions for each of the book’s fourteen chapters.
  • A Mile Marker for each chapter: what you recognized about yourself, and what you’ll choose to do differently.
  • A fillable PDF. Type your answers and save it privately, or print it and write by hand.

What you write stays on your own device. We never see it.

We’ll email you the journal and send occasional notes from Brent and Angela. Unsubscribe anytime.

For Brent & AngelaThis is the page the book points to (BuiltForMoreInstitute.com/journal). It describes the full journal you said will be ready by launch; for now the download is Chapter One, rebuilt from your Word file as a fillable PDF with the same questions and layout. Each answer gets a writing box, because ruled lines don’t line up with typed text in every PDF app. A name and email are required, like Discover.
